review_notes: The cleaned Commons/NOAA satellite segment shows active fire detections and bright fire-front regions rapidly expanding and migrating across frames. A single frame only shows isolated hotspots; the named concept requires observing the front propagation over time. The source page double-checks strong-wind/cold-front forcing, while the video itself provides the front-growth evidence. Logo, audio, and metadata were removed.

The no-label Texas wildfire clip also shows rapid wildfire expansion, but it targets the same concept as the stronger Ranger Road pass sample and is only about three seconds long. Reject as duplicate backup rather than repeating the concept.

The GIF repeats near-identical satellite frames of Soufriere Hills and does not show a visually decisive dome-collapse sequence or collapse-generated plume/flow evolution. Accepting Lava Dome Collapse would rely on the filename/source category rather than video evidence.
